title: Proton: Probing Schema Linking Information from Pre-trained Language Models for Text-to-SQL Parsing

problem.claim: Text-to-SQL parsers need to recognize mentions of unseen columns or tables when generating SQL for new databases.

gap.claim: Commonly used rule-based schema-linking methods may not robustly capture semantic correspondences when surface forms of mentions and entities differ.

contributions.claim: A probing framework elicits relational structures from large-scale pre-trained language models using the Poincaré distance metric.
The induced relations augment graph-based parsers for schema linking.
The probing procedure is unsupervised and requires no additional parameters.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their framework as a novel approach for eliciting relational structures from pre-trained language models through probing.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that probing relations robustly capture semantic correspondences even when surface forms differ.
The authors report state-of-the-art performance on three benchmarks in extensive experiments.
The authors report qualitative empirical verification that the probing procedure finds desired relational structures.

narrative_sequence.summary: Schema linking is identified as critical for applying text-to-SQL parsers to new databases.
The framework probes pre-trained language models for relational structures using Poincaré distance and uses them to augment graph-based parsers.
The authors report that the probed relations capture semantic correspondences despite differing surface forms.
The probing procedure is described as unsupervised and parameter-free.
The authors report benchmark performance and qualitative analysis supporting the framework.

source_observation.claim: Probing relations are reported to capture semantic correspondences when surface forms differ.

interpretation.claim: Latent relational information from pre-trained models may complement surface-form matching for schema linking.

application.claim: For text-to-SQL systems, consider augmenting rule-based schema linking with model-derived relational signals.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how performance varies across database domains or mention types.

source_observation.claim: The probing procedure is described as unsupervised and requiring no additional parameters.

interpretation.claim: Schema-linking enhancements may be possible without adding supervised training parameters.

application.claim: When extending an existing parser, evaluate parameter-free auxiliary procedures as a low-overhead integration option.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify computational cost, implementation constraints, or sensitivity to the chosen language model.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the three benchmarks.
The abstract does not report numerical results or baseline comparisons.
The abstract does not describe the probing procedure in implementation detail.
The abstract does not specify the qualitative analysis protocol.
